name: Sovereign debt stress
summary: France–Bund 10-year spread about 147bp on 10 Nov, back below the 150bp Alert line from a 174.6bp peak on 22 Oct
state: France's 10-year yield fell to 4.70% on 10 Nov, a six-week low, before closing near 4.75% and holding there on 11 Nov, against about 3.28% on the German Bund (Trading Economics). That puts the spread near 147bp, below the 150bp Alert line and down from 152.9bp on 9 Nov and a 174.6bp peak on 22 Oct. The spread remains in the 80–150bp Watch band amid French political and fiscal uncertainty; no failed G7 auction or emergency ECB buying was found as of 11 Nov.
for_you: Higher French borrowing costs tend to feed through to mortgage and business loan rates in France and can weigh on the euro. Public budgets face pressure as more goes on interest.
rubric_hit: France–Bund ~147bp within 80–150bp Watch band, below 150bp Alert line

why: When big governments struggle to borrow, it raises everyone's costs and can force sudden austerity or money-printing.
drivers: Deficits, auction demand, ratings actions, political shocks, long-end yields.

rubric.alert: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.
rubric.watch: G7 30-year yields at multi-decade highs, a G7 downgrade, or France–Bund 80–150bp / Italy–Bund 150–250bp.
rubric.normal: Auctions orderly; France–Bund spread < 80bp; Italy–Bund < 150bp; no G7 downgrades this month.
